cover.alt: Watchmaker's maintenance bench with a separate spare mechanism for recovery

figures.title: Turn maintenance into recurring checks
figures.summary: Different tasks run at different intervals in the article's schedule.

items.label: Continuous
items.detail: Monitor availability and keep spam protection active.

items.label: Daily or weekly
items.detail: Run backups appropriate to the site's data-change rate.

items.label: Monthly
items.detail: Check certificates, security scans and activity logs.

items.label: Quarterly
items.detail: Review accounts and remove unnecessary access.

figures.caption: The maintenance cadence proposed in this article; adapt it to the system's actual risk and recovery needs.

figures.title: A backup needs a recovery check
figures.summary: Having a file is different from knowing the site can be restored.

items.label: Separate copy
items.detail: Store backups away from the live server.

items.label: Recent data
items.detail: Confirm the backup contains the content and data you need.

items.label: Restore rehearsal
items.detail: Test the recovery process instead of assuming it works.

items.label: Working deployment
items.detail: Verify the restored site or static build actually runs.

items.label: Reachable alert
items.detail: Make sure an outage reaches the person responsible.

figures.caption: Recovery and monitoring checks derived from the article's backup and uptime sections.
